subject: Clarify: admin activity log extract — redaction & sampling scope
messages:
From: Lena Morales <lena@blackpinehealth.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Admin activity extract — redaction & sampling questions

Hi Sean,

Thanks again for the quick demo last week. Our security team is preparing the SIG/SOC2 evidence bundle and we need to confirm the scope and delivery format for Redwood's admin-activity/admin-audit logs. Can you confirm the following items so we can lock the checklist?

- What event types are included in the standard admin-activity extract (e.g., admin sign-in, role change, API key create/revoke, model-version deploy, config change)?
- Retention windows you can export for: 30/90/365 days — do you provide on-demand slices or only continuous streams?
- Do you support per-user PII redaction (email/user-id redaction) at export time, or do we need to request a scrubbed copy and a separate raw copy?
- Sampling: for very large tenants we may request sampled snapshots. Is there a supported sampling strategy (time-bound, hashed-subject, per-user rate)?
- Delivery formats we accept: NDJSON, compressed CSV, or signed tarball with checksum — which do you produce?

I've attached our evidence_request_template.pdf to show what the auditor will expect. We're trying to avoid extra back-and-forth; if you can provide a short export options matrix and preferred redaction workflow that would be ideal.

Lena Morales
Sr. Information Security Manager
Black Pine Health

Attachment: evidence_request_template.pdf (PDF, 248KB)

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Morales <lena@blackpinehealth.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2026 10:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Admin activity extract — redaction & sampling questions

Lena — thanks for the clear list. Below is a concise mapping to what we can deliver today and the typical trade-offs. Happy to jump on a 20-min call if helpful.

Quick answers (summary):
- Event types: our standard admin-activity export includes: operator sign-in/auth events, role/grant changes, API key lifecycle (create/revoke), model deploy/rollback events, routing/policy changes, console UI actions (create/delete routes), and operator-initiated data exports. We DO NOT include application-level user prompts or generated content in this export — those are in separate tracers.
- Retention/export slices: we offer on-demand time-window exports for any contiguous window up to your account retention cap (default 365 days for enterprise). For very large windows we can stage a streaming export.
- Redaction: we support configurable redaction at export time. Options: (1) redact emails/usernames with a deterministic hash, (2) pseudonymize to stable IDs, or (3) provide raw plus a scrubbed copy under an elevated request/attestation.
- Sampling: supported strategies — time-window sampling, deterministic-hash sampling (consistent across exports), and per-user-rate throttled sampling. For auditor reproducibility we recommend deterministic-hash sampling so rows for the same operator resolve consistently across runs.
- Formats/delivery: NDJSON.gz or CSV.gz inside a signed tarball with an accompanying SHA256 manifest file. We can also push to an S3 pre-signed URL or SFTP endpoint depending on your compliance controls.

I attached a short example manifest (admin_event_manifest_sample.csv) showing field names and a sample hashed_user_id column. Operational notes below.

Operational notes / caveats:
- Timestamps: events include both event_time (canonical UTC) and ingestion_time. We normalize timezone on export but keep original timestamps as metadata.
- KV/cache keys: we do not export raw KV cache contents; we log cache evictions and operator actions that clear caches.
- Live rollbacks: for rolling deployments there may be multiple deploy events for the same model_id — we include full event context but not binary model artifacts.
- HMAC checksums: each archive includes a signed manifest; if you require an attestation signed by Redwood legal, let us know and we'll route to contracts.

Next steps: if the deterministic-hash sampling + NDJSON tarball looks good, we can prepare a 7-day sample export to validate format against your auditors.

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: admin_event_manifest_sample.csv (CSV, 14KB)

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Morales <lena@blackpinehealth.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2026 11:33:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Admin activity extract — redaction & sampling questions

Lena / Sean — adding a few implementation details from ops that often matter for SOC/SIG reviewers.

- Redaction mechanics: our export pipeline applies redaction rules as a final step in the artifact staging area (post-ingest). Deterministic hashing uses a per-customer salt (rotated quarterly). We can provide the salt rotation schedule and salt-hash algorithm doc (SHA-256 HMAC) to auditors under NDA.
- De-duplication & ordering: exports preserve event ordering by event_time. We also include an event_id stable across retries to help auditors dedupe ingestion duplicates.
- Data minimization / PII: for fields that are free-text (operator notes), we offer an optional NLP-based PII scrub that redacts emails/phone numbers. This is computational and has a small false-negative rate; auditors usually want the raw copy under elevated request.
- Sampling reproducibility: deterministic-hash sampling is the only way we guarantee identical results across repeated exports. Time-window sampling is easier but won't be identical if you request overlapping windows with ongoing events.
- Delivery handshake: preferred: S3 pre-signed + manifest + signature. Alternative for high-security tenants: push to SFTP + PGP-encrypted tarball.

If Black Pine needs a short attestation text to include in the evidence bundle that describes our redaction workflow and salt rotation, we can draft a one-paragraph statement for review.

Kimberly Park
Product Security Lead, Redwood Inference

Thanks Sean / Kimberly — this is very helpful. A couple quick follow-ups before we sign off:

1) For the auditor we will request: (a) a 7-day deterministic-hash sample in NDJSON.gz, (b) the salt rotation cadence doc, and (c) a short one-paragraph attestation about the redaction pipeline. Can you confirm turnaround for the 7-day sample?
2) For delivery, can Redwood push to our S3 staging bucket (we will provide role-based access) or do you prefer we provide a pre-signed URL?

If timeline permits we would like the sample by next Tuesday (2026-04-21) to include in the evidence package. If you can confirm estimates and a contact for S3 access handshake I'll escalate the request to procurement.

Appreciate the quick answers — looking forward to the sample and the attestation paragraph.

Lena
